newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Congress panel begins re-election debate.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Congress panel begins re-election debate.

text.p: A committee in Brazil's Chamber of Deputies kicked off discussions of a constitutional amendment that would give President Fernando Henrique Cardoso the chance of a second term, a congressional official said.
"The meeting has begun," the official said.
The committee has up to 40 sessions, each equivalent to a working day, to vote on the proposed constitutional amendment.

Observers say the amendment faces few hurdles in its committee stage. However, it faces a stiff test on the floor of the lower house where, if approved by the committee, it will require two three-fifths majorities.
The bill is expected to reach the floor of the lower house in January.
The amendment would allow presidents, state governors and mayors to stand for a second term. Brazil's constitution limits holders of executive office to one term.
